acceptedSamples.description: Full warm dark Athas window on forest desktop. Actions selected; nine visible run rows. Right document remains the successful openssl CI run: six metadata fields, Bun job with eight visible successful steps and 2 more steps, partially visible Rust job header. Top and bottom toolbars present.
Cursor hovers Prepare release in Actions. The already-open right CI document is unchanged.
Actions status filter menu is opening below the filter icon. All Runs, In Progress, Successful and Failed are visible.
Actions filter menu fully open. All Runs carries the checkmark; no other option is shown selected. Persistent CI detail remains unchanged.
Issues clicked. The sidebar horizontally slides from Actions to Issues; both list panes are visible during transition, active tab label expands.
Issues active. Ten visible issue rows with author avatars and issue numbers; first row hovered. Search, add and filter stay in place. Right CI document remains open.
Pull Requests icon hovered/clicked while Issues is still visible. Tooltip names Pull Requests; sidebar transition starts.
Pull Requests active at list top; first openssl PR hovered. PR rows include number, author and branch strips. Same right CI document.

Only the Pull Requests list has scrolled downward about 70 source-scaled pixels. First branch strip partly clipped at viewport top; third PR hovered. Top navigation and right CI document remain fixed.
Pull Requests list restored to top. Cursor moves toward Search; no search text is entered and no detail is opened.
Issues active again with third row hover. Same six metadata fields and Bun job on right.
Cursor hovers Bun job card, slightly changing its background. Sidebar remains Issues; no Log click, execution or right-panel scroll is confirmed.
Final Issues sidebar and original successful workflow detail held in the same application window; cursor has left the hovered region.

mechanisms: One continuous desktop software window with persistent top toolbar, bottom status bar, sidebar and right document.
Three icon-and-label sidebar tabs. Only active label is expanded; horizontal pane slide moves Actions to Issues to Pull Requests and back to Issues.
Actions status filter opens/closes with All Runs checked; four visible options retained without inventing a selection change.
Actions, Issues and PR row hover responses; PR list alone scrolls down and returns to top.
Open CI workflow survives sidebar navigation: title, Success and 2 jobs, six metadata fields, Bun task, eight successful visible steps, 2 more steps and partial Rust header.
Final Bun job hover and reading hold; no new document opening or actual execution is demonstrated.
differences: Source 2170x1592 desktop adapted to editable 1920x1080 horizontal layout; 14.127621s actions expanded to 26s for readable filter, lists and workflow.
Independent original SVG icons, cartoon avatars and blurred abstract forest geometry replace all source photos/media pixels.
Sidebar long titles retain visible truncation instead of guessing missing source words.
Source release/CI subtitle and branch information retained, with two-line compact later Actions rows; first two runs preserve their three visible lines.
Repository name, open run title and branch are editable text objects shared consistently across their corresponding regions.
No backend, GitHub integration or filter/search execution is represented as real.
unknowns: Actual GitHub authentication, network calls, run execution, repository permissions and service implementation are not observable.
Filter option result, search result, add action and Log/external/copy action outcomes are not demonstrated.
Some clipped issue/PR titles and hidden Rust job content cannot be fully read; no hidden content is reconstructed.
No right-panel scroll, new PR/issue detail opening or active task execution is confirmed.
works.sourceObservationMethod: Exact source card modal and original href read; original remote video actually paused/viewed at accepted decoded samples. No remote pixels distributed. Not a full original source-code replica or real service execution.
